claims.text: Controlled nitridation of an elemental Cr coating will form a thin CrN layer at or near the Cr/zirconium interface.
An interfacial CrN layer will retard Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Retarding Cr–Zr interdiffusion will enhance coating integrity under high-temperature steam accident conditions.
The nitridated coating will preserve protection under normal subcritical-water conditions.
A nitrogen-containing heat treatment can transform part of the elemental Cr coating into CrN while preferentially producing a barrier near the Cr–Zr interface.
CrN is more thermodynamically stable against Cr–Zr interdiffusion than elemental Cr.
CrN has lower relevant elemental diffusivity than elemental Cr.
The lower diffusivity of CrN enables it to act as a barrier to high-temperature intermixing of Cr and Zr.
Limiting high-temperature Cr–Zr intermixing will preserve coating integrity.
The CrN barrier can limit interdiffusion while retaining adequate oxidation protection.
The nitridated coating will have a lower interfacial diffusion rate than an unmodified elemental-Cr-coated zirconium-alloy baseline.
The nitridated coating will exhibit greater durability than the unmodified baseline in high-temperature steam.
The nitridated coating will maintain oxidation behavior relative to the unmodified baseline under subcritical-water exposure.
